Account Sieve and ManageSieve

Each account can store 32 named Sieve scripts in mail.db, with one active script. An empty active name disables Sieve. Uploads compile the whole script before changing stored data, including replacements of active scripts.

The interpreter is Rust inside maild with no subprocess, filesystem or network access. The maintained Stalwart sieve-rs was evaluated first: its AGPL licence fails MixOS's permissive dependency policy. No suitable maintained permissive Rust interpreter was found. This implementation uses the existing MIME parser and native mail store without new dependencies.

Language

Base commands are require, if/elsif/else, stop, keep, discard and redirect. Tests are address, header, exists, size, allof, anyof, not, true and false. Quoted and text: multi-line strings, hash and bracketed comments, :is/:contains/:matches, i;ascii-casemap and i;octet are supported.

Extensions: fileinto, mailbox (fileinto :create), envelope, imap4flags, copy, body, variables, vacation, relational, comparator-i;ascii-numeric, reject, ereject and index. Required capabilities must precede executable statements. Unknown commands/tags/capabilities are refused, including in dead branches. date/currentdate are deferred and not advertised.

require ["fileinto", "mailbox", "imap4flags", "body"];
if header :is "X-Mixos-Spam-Verdict" "SPAM" {
    fileinto :create "Spam";
    stop;
}
if body :text :contains "release announcement" {
    fileinto :create :flags "\\Flagged" "Releases";
}

fileinto uses slash-separated mailbox paths; INBOX resolves by role. :create creates missing parents. Missing destinations without :create keep the message at its default destination. Flags map to the same MDS flags and validated user keywords as IMAP/JMAP. File actions snapshot the current flags. :copy preserves implicit keep. Variables support substitution, wildcard captures, case modifiers, wildcard quoting and length.

body uses decoded MIME text, strips HTML markup for :text, selects MIME types with :content, and exposes the untransformed body with :raw. Relational :value/:count support gt, ge, lt, le, eq, ne; :count requires i;ascii-numeric. Header :index N selects one occurrence, with :last counting from the end.

Delivery and policy

SMTP classifies spam, runs the global Mix inbound_filter, then runs account Sieve. This preserves the existing filter's spam inputs. The Mix destination, or classifier Inbox/Junk default, is Sieve's keep destination. The stored message has daemon-generated X-Mixos-Spam-Verdict and X-Mixos-Spam-Score headers; incoming copies are removed. Verdicts are HAM, SPAM or UNKNOWN when classification is disabled or fails. JMAP/native Bus submissions also run recipient Sieve on local delivery, with Inbox as keep, without rerunning the inbound classifier or global Mix filter.

Evaluation produces a complete action plan. Syntax/runtime errors, invalid flags, missing destinations and refused redirects cancel the plan and keep the message. Limits: 64 KiB per script, 10,000 evaluation/matching/allocation steps, 64 filing/redirect actions, 1 MiB of variables and four redirects. Matching charges for scanned bytes as well as instructions. Local redirects run the destination's script; the four-hop header also bounds remote loops. A forged high hop count can suppress forwarding but never grants extra hops.

reject/ereject return SMTP 550 5.7.1 after DATA for a single normal recipient. Mixed-recipient/asynchronous delivery instead queues a DSN with a null reverse path. DSNs to null/unverified senders are suppressed to prevent backscatter. Combining reject with filing, redirect, discard or vacation is a runtime error and keeps the original message.

Off-site redirects default to refused. sieve_external_domains lists exact account domains allowed to redirect to non-local addresses. It also enables those domains' Sieve vacation replies to non-local senders. This is operator configuration, never script data. Local destinations must be account addresses.

Vacation supports :days (1..31, default 7), :addresses, :subject, :from :handle and :mime entities. :from must be the account address. :addresses recognises additional To/Cc recipient identities; it does not authorise sender spoofing. Replies require verified ingress and a recognised To/Cc identity. Spam, null senders, self-mail, list/bulk mail and automatic responses receive no reply. A durable atomic sender/response-handle stamp permits one reply per interval across concurrent deliveries and restarts. Replies use a null reverse path, Auto-Submitted: auto-replied, and the native outbound queue. Its worker selects the account domain's DKIM signer; absent signing configuration retains the existing unsigned behaviour. An active Sieve script takes ownership of automatic responses; the older JMAP VacationResponse runs only without an active Sieve script, preventing two automatic replies to the same message.

ManageSieve

Disabled by default. In the maild configuration:

sieve_listen: ["192.0.2.10:4190"]
sieve_implicit_tls: false
sieve_external_domains: []

false selects RFC 5804 STARTTLS, the normal mode on 4190; true selects implicit TLS. Both share SMTP/IMAP's TLS identities, SNI resolver and hot-reload slot. Enabling the listener without TLS material fails startup. Port 4190 needs no new unit privileges. NodeConfig fallback leaves this optional listener off; set the keys in the maild configuration used by the daemon.

Commands: CAPABILITY, AUTHENTICATE PLAIN/LOGIN, LISTSCRIPTS, GETSCRIPT, PUTSCRIPT, CHECKSCRIPT, SETACTIVE, DELETESCRIPT, RENAMESCRIPT, HAVESPACE, NOOP, LOGOUT. Authentication and script access require TLS. Passwords use the shared account verifier. PLAIN authorisation identity must be empty or equal the login identity. Only the authenticated account's scripts are accessible. Uploads accept quoted strings and non-synchronising octet literals ({N+}). Malformed/oversized frames close the session. Limits: 128 connections, 180-second pre-authentication and 30-minute authenticated command timeouts, 30-second TLS/authentication timeout, three failed logins. STARTTLS discards buffered plaintext commands.

Bus editing and versions

Like maild's existing operator commands, broker callers select an account; ManageSieve instead enforces authenticated account isolation.

CommandRequestResponse
maild.sieve.listaccountscripts: name, version, active, size
maild.sieve.getaccount, namename, version, active, source
maild.sieve.putaccount, name, source, optional expected_versionnew version
maild.sieve.activateaccount, name (empty disables)active name

Account identifiers are email addresses. PUT's optional version guard uses zero for a new script and refuses stale writes. Replacements preserve active state. sieve_scripts stores current source; sieve_versions retains the latest 16 revisions per name. Versions are never reused after deletion. ManageSieve uses the RFC's last-writer-wins editing semantics. Account deletion cascades to all script/version/vacation-stamp rows.
